The method

Three things a program has to leave behind.

01

A lure your technician can send before lunch.

Finance gets the invoice. HR gets the benefits note. English, Spanish, or Turkish. The mail is marked as a simulation after the click, never as a consumer drill.

02

A brief you can drop into the QBR.

Each tenant gets a one-page record: click rate falling, who reported, what they finished. That is the leave-behind your account manager already knows how to sell.

03

Your logo. Not ours.

The quarterly phishing record is white-labeled. Brokers and auditors see the MSP. PhishSim stays off the cover.

The book

A book of tenants, not a retail signup.

MSPs and MSSPs provision a client, keep ConnectWise and Halo quiet on simulations, and put their own domain on the portal. The end customer buys from you. We stay in the wholesale layer.

Notes from the practice
01 · Against the cartoon

A ninja is a costume.

Phishing is a letter, a voice, a code on a door. The site should look like the file you hand a broker, not a booth graphic.

02 · Against the seat

Margin should widen.

Platforms that bill per person punish the firm for winning work. This engagement does the opposite.

03 · Against the demo

Ten minutes, then the mail.

Import the list. Send the lure. Teach the miss. Print the record. If that takes a procurement cycle, it is the wrong instrument.
